sentences.text:
2. Let necessary insertion in the cause title of the present writ petition be made by learned counsel for the petitioner in course of the day.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner undertakes to serve two copies of the present writ petition to Mrs. Sweety Topno, learned counsel for the respondent no. 6.
4.

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction upon the concerned respondents to pay the balance amount of compensation to the petitioner for acquisition of his land appertaining to Jamabandi No. 33, Daag No./Survey Plot Nos. 129, 130, 131, 135, 136 & 137, measuring an area of 0.4510, 0.4454, 0.9643, 0.2719, 0.3327 & 0.5912 acres respectively of Mouza- Patharia, Balapokhar,
Thana No. 32, Thana-Taljhari, District- Sahebganj for widening and realignment of NH-80 (KM 197 Lode Hembrom vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71217493/
1 to KM 260).
5.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the aforesaid land is recorded in the name of Bhoju Hembrom and Baijal Hembrom.
After amicable partition, the said land came in exclusive possession of Baijal Hembrom, who died leaving behind his two sons namely, Harmu Hembrom and Kode Hembrom.
Thereafter, Kode Hembrom died leaving behind his only son Ragda Hembrom.
The petitioner is the son of Ragda Hembrom and great grandson of Baijal Hembrom (since deceased).

In the process of acquisition of the said land, Land Acquisition Case No. 51/2016-17 was initiated and notices under Section 3-H of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 1956') [wrongly mentioned as Section 37(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 in the said notice - Annexure-1 series to the writ petition] were issued to the petitioner by the respondent no. 4 - the District Land Acquisition Officer, Sahebganj-cum-Competent Authority under the Act, 1956 fixing total compensation amount of Rs.98,02,516.44.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The grievance of the petitioner is that out of the said total compensation amount, only Rs.43,17,597/- has been paid to him, however, the balance amount of Rs.54,84,919.44 has not been paid despite several representations made to the authorities in this regard.
Under the said compelling circumstance, the petitioner has preferred the present writ petition.

6. Mr. Praveen Akhauri, learned SC (Mines)-I appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 to 5 and Mrs. Sweety Topno, learned counsel for the respondent No. 6, jointly submit that the aforesaid contention of the petitioner is required to be factually examined by the respondent No. 4 and hence,
if he prefers a fresh application before the said respondent in this regard, an appropriate decision will be taken within a time frame.
7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of the prayer made in the present writ petition, without entering into the merit of the petitioner's aforesaid contention, he is given liberty to prefer a fresh application before the respondent No. 4 in this regard.

On receipt of the said application, the respondent No. 4, after verifying the relevant records and on providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner/his representative, shall take an appropriate informed decision within one month from the date of filing of the said application.
8. The present writ petition is accordingly disposed of with aforesaid liberty and direction.
(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Manish Lode Hembrom vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71217493/
